about: What the founder wants the cloud transcript provider measured on (ADR-039). Entries point at files that already exist in the repository's generated or committed test sets where one exists; where none exists the entry says so. Nothing here is uploaded unless the founder runs the harness with --i-have-founder-approval and names the entries.
privateRule: Every file under web/tests/media/real/ is the founder's own video: private: true, refused without --allow-private (the harness also enforces this by path, whatever this file says).

generated.web/tests/media/speech/manifest-real.jso: node web/spike/asr/prepare-english.mjs, then node web/scripts/transcript/prepare-realistic.mjs --set=dev and --set=val (downloads openly licensed sources: AMI CC BY 4.0, Earnings-22 CC BY-SA 4.0, LibriSpeech CC BY 4.0, Wikimedia Commons music; see web/tests/media/SPEECH_SOURCE.md)
generated.web/tests/media/speech/manifest.json: node web/spike/asr/prepare-speech.mjs (FLEURS, CC BY 4.0: 12 Turkish and 6 English read sentences)

entries.title: One read English sentence (9.6 s) — the only speech file committed to the repository; use it for the very first real call
entries.reference: It was ruled by the "Vichy" French. These were French people who had made peace with the Germans in 1940 and worked with the invaders instead of fighting them.

entries.title: Earnings-22 call 4474229, whole call, 51 minutes (prepared remarks + questions, telephone sound, accents)
entries.note: On device (ADR-036, 7 Oct): WER normalised base 14.7 %, turbo 11.1 %. Reference has no word times and no speaker count.

entries.title: AMI IS1009a, headset mix, 14 minutes: four people, overlaps, fillers, laughter
entries.note: On device: WER normalised base 25.5 %, turbo 21.9 %; speech written 96.6 % / 99.4 %. Word times: manual (AMI).

entries.title: The same meeting (AMI IS1009a) from ONE far table microphone: quiet, reverberant
entries.note: On device: WER normalised base 34.2 %, turbo 25.8 %.

entries.title: AMI TS3003a 11:00–16:00 with music under the talking at SNR 10 dB, 5 minutes
entries.note: On device: WER normalised base 54.8 %, turbo 22.4 %. The weakest on-device case. How many of the meeting's four people speak inside this stretch was not counted, so no expected speaker count.

entries.title: Clean speech with music and everyday sounds butted against it: nothing may be written inside the marked gaps
entries.note: On device: 0 words in the gaps. approxDurationS is a guess (the generated manifest has the exact length); the cloud route must not be worse at inventing text.

entries.title: Earnings-22 call 4481221, Indian accent, 21 minutes
entries.note: On device: WER normalised base 15.7 %, turbo 10.9 %. Optional: leave it out to stay well under the ceiling.

entries.title: One read Turkish sentence (FLEURS tr_tr)
entries.note: Read speech only. tr-02 … tr-12 exist in the same set and can be named on the command line by path. approxDurationS is a guess.

entries.title: A read Turkish sentence under synthetic music at SNR 5 dB (September spike clip noisy-03)
Spontaneous Turkish conversation, 10–20 minutes, with a reference transcript
entries.howToGet: no openly licensed, transcribed conversational Turkish recording is in the repository's sets; needs a file (e.g. a recording the founder makes and transcribes, or an open corpus to be found and licence-checked)

entries.title: Read Japanese sentences (FLEURS ja_jp), scored by character error rate
entries.howToGet: not generated today: prepare-speech.mjs fetches only tr_tr and en_us; the same script with a ja_jp range would produce it (FLEURS, CC BY 4.0)

entries.title: Spontaneous Japanese conversation with a reference transcript
entries.howToGet: needs a file; no source chosen

entries.title: Exactly two people talking over each other, with word times and who-said-what
entries.howToGet: needs a file. Can be built rights-clean from two LibriSpeech readers mixed with a known overlap (word times and speaker of every word are then known exactly); prepare-realistic.mjs has the building blocks but no such clip today. Until then meeting-overlap-4 (four speakers) is the nearest case.
